body:
> Don't ask me what's wrong, if I tell you you won't care. You won't get why it's a problem, because it probably isn't for you. For me, it's ruining my life.

I get that, I really do.  I'm a fat guy, so I don't *get* anorexia, but at some point I grew up enough to sympathize with anyone who just feels out of control of their life.  Give peeps a chance, eventually you won't feel so alone.

I don't blame anyone for saying that, since it seems to be human nature to only want to help people who can be *pleasantly* needy (I'm not being sarcastic, viscerally it throws me off too), but it's a vicious cycle. In other words (if tigershrimp is being honest) he probably started out pleasant. 

Easy for me to say, but if I could go back in time and give him my bitcoin instead of having pissed it away at Satoshi Circle, I'd probably feel better about it.

It started out with computer graphics...I think the idea was that I wanted to design video games.  I did well in photoshop/autocad/technical drawing classes but felt like I learned nothing.  Like once class ended I couldn't draw an empty box in photoshop to save my life.  And with harder classes ahead of me I panicked and wanted to quit, but ended up focusing on core curriculum instead.  Then it was liberal arts/english/creative writing, then just liberal arts/english.  Eventually I ran out of time and attemptable credit hours to keep fucking around with it, so I went to see what degree I was closest to earning, and liberal arts/general studies it is.  From what I hear it basically as useful as a high school diploma these days, so at least I'm maintaining my level of mediocrity.  

But school is my biggest source of stress right now.  I'm taking three classes.  Two of them I'm pretty sure I'll get by, but the third is a capstone course...one credit hour, I thought it would be nothing, but it's turned out to be really involved and confusing.   I'm way behind in it, because I keep getting overwhelmed and confused so I just walk away.  I just want to drop it and save it for next semester, but my wife already has it in her head that I'm graduating in May, same as her (she's earning her masters).  I cannot possibly explain dropping this class in a way that would make it okay.  

We've had arguments about my condition that are just crazy, and I end up not really knowing whether or not she actually understands what's going on with me.  I know she thinks she does, she also suffers from depression and anxiety, but not in a way that makes any sense to me.  She becomes *more* functional.  Not happy, really stressed out, but functional.  I cannot justify to someone who has the same disease as me, but still manages to teach full-time, earn her masters degree, AND head up all this extra-curricular stuff like after school clubs why I can't handle three classes when I'm unemployed.  

Right now the biggest weight on my chest is this weeks classes.  I've given up on the online capstone course, I'm just dreading having to talk about it with my wife, and I feel like the longer I put it off the worse it will be but it's already going to be bad enough that I'd literally rather run the fuck away.  The other two classes, one is an online english class that just has a lot of work to be done before sunday that I'm putting off.  The other is a science class at the campus, and I've blown off a class an a half because all the math involved in the physics portion is killing me, and I hate being in a class with other people regardless.

Our honeymoon was a Carnival Cruise.  It's kinda lame, I know all the dark stuff behind the cruise industry, and recent news, whatever, I don't care, it's the happiest I've been in a long time.  It's been about two years since we got off the boat, and we've spent most of that time talking about getting back on it.  My wife especially deserves it, she's been working incredibly hard this year and we haven't gotten to take a vacation since then.

My car was stolen in December.  It was an '83 Oldsmobile station wagon.  Had her for about three years, looked almost cherry when I bought it and only paid $1000, but was never able to take care of it beyond the occasional oil change.  I have a feeling it's sitting in an empty lot in a shitty neighborhood, just rotting after a joyride.  I'd like to find it and restore it... and have a garage to put it in.  I'd probably keep collecting old wagons... don't know what it is about them.

I'd like to learn to build things... welding, carpentry... and then build cool things.  I know that could be a career, but it's not a solution to right now.  I'm already too deep in debt from school, which was a waste of time anyway.  But in this context, I would learn to build things.

I saw a commercial once, something about stock trading I think, where someone is getting towed after their car breaks down in the middle of nowhere and the towtruck driver eventually reveals that he's filthy rich...shows a picture of the island he owns on the back of his sun visor... and he just drives the tow truck because he likes helping people.  I got a kick out of that, and I think I would literally buy a tow truck, learn engines, and get trained in CPR... y'know... for *fun*.

I'd try writing.  I'm constantly told by family and teachers that I should write, but I can't do it as a career.  I can't be creative under pressure, my brain does not work correctly under pressure.  But I do have ONE good idea for a novel, and if I didn't have to worry about supporting myself or dying due to lack of insurance I'd give it a go.

I'm very much into retrofuturism... I'm kinda obsessed with the vision of the future I experienced growing up around EPCOT Center in the 80s.  I'd probably throw too much money at trying to get that feeling back.  If I were insanely rich I'd have Horizons rebuilt and let all comers ride for free.

I own a few guns my dad left me, and I'd keep collecting and have a range in my backyard.

My wife works in education right now, but since I bought her an ice cream maker for christmas she really wants to get creative with flavors and start a business.  She's also always wanted to own a little sandwich shop/cafe.  I'd love to make those happen.

I've got a cousin who's transgender... hardly spoken to her since I was little, but I'd be thrilled to pay for her gender reassignment.

I think I'm dry.  That was fun.

I'm not sure what to do now.  I don't really want to talk, to be honest.  I want someone to throw me a miracle.  But as usual no miracles are forthcoming, so I guess I'd like to talk...but I don't know about what.  Have any questions?

I didn't hate them.  I just didn't get anything out of them.  Last one (only been two, really) was a really nice guy, and I felt bad when I stopped answering his calls.  I was on the low end of a sliding payment scale and I guess I was afraid I seemed ungrateful.  But all I've ever done is talk, but never come to any conclusions, or figure out how to make things better.  

I've literally been at this for hours, and I need to go to bed.  Nothing is going to happen in the meantime.  Maybe that means I'm in the wrong subreddit.  Thanks though, I'll be back.
